instagram:
Paper trade today. My funded account got the day off.

Short 2 ES at 7,345.25. My stop was 4 points from entry, at 7,349.25.

Price dropped close to 9 points first. Then it climbed all the way back to 7,348.50, three quarters of a point from the stop. I stayed in.

The target at 7,335.00 filled on the next push down: 10.25 points on 2 contracts, +$1,025 on paper, before fees.

When a trade comes back that close to your stop, what do you do: hold it, cut it, or move the stop?

facebook:
I sat out on my funded account today and traded on paper instead.

The trade: short 2 ES from 7,345.25, stop 4 points away at 7,349.25, target 7,335.00.

It started well. Price fell nearly 9 points in my favor. Then it turned and climbed back to 7,348.50, less than a point from stopping me out.

The stop never filled. Price rolled over again and reached 7,335.00 for 10.25 points on both contracts. That's +$1,025 on paper, before fees.

Same stop as always, 4 points from where I got in.

Have you ever been a tick or two from your stop and still ended up at your target?
